name: Projection
definition: Snapshot summary of each plane's claims as of its last visit.
example: A dated summary says the button was not keyboard accessible when last checked.

name: Intent
definition: What the owner wants, with reasons, boundaries, corrections and confirmation status.
example: The owner wants a keyboard-accessible button so visitors can use it without a mouse.

name: Enduring Context
definition: Our knowledge of what exists, what Canon and Grounding say exists or should change, and Intent and what to do with it.
example: The team knows the button currently misses keyboard focus and understands the owner's requested outcome.

name: Grounding
definition: Evidence and proofs used to establish and support the authoritative source of truth.
example: A recorded keyboard test on a named version shows whether the button receives focus.

name: Canon
definition: The authoritative source of truth for the target: what governs.
example: The assigned acceptance condition says the button must be operable by keyboard.

name: Actuality
definition: What exists and is being worked on.
example: The running button receives focus and can be activated with the keyboard.
